That "Grass Bubble" is actually when rainwater or water in general can't properly go through the ground. You've got your layers of soil on the upper most part where grass it, then tiny little rocks and pebbles, and then finally big rocks way down. As water falls the ground naturally soaks it up and drains it, so you don't have puddles or muddy spots. However when there is too much water it clogs the layers up between the big rocks, and tiny little rocks and pebbles. That's how you get grass bubbles. I am an infant/toddler teacher at a daycare center, so I've seen the crying more than a few times.  Here they are, being put in an unfamiliar place, with unfamiliar people, with out their comfort zone (mommy). My advice would to keep bringing him. If you stop bringing him, he will never learn to branch off from you or learn that it's okay for mommy to be gone, because I know she will be back. He needs to learn to trust others. He needs that social interaction with other kids and adults other than his immediate family. It's completely normal that he cried, and if you waited awhile and then bring him back, he'll still cry. Try to bring him as often as you can. Play there with him. Introduce him to the workers, talk to them while your holding him, try to let them hold him while you talk, then hold him again. -Might seem strange, but let Jackson see you hug them.- Stay a little while until he's comfortable enough that he can walk across the room to play with out bringing you with him. When he gets to the point of playing where he's not paying any attention, you can leave. Don't call his attention and say bye, just sneak away. Eventually, as he becomes more comfortable with the daycare, you'll have no problem with dropping him off.
